newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal firm on corn gains, soyoil mixed.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal firm on corn gains, soyoil mixed.

text.p: CBOT soymeal futures were firm at midsession, in line with gains in corn, while soyoil futures were mixed, traders said.
"Soybean complex will not stand still with corn going up," a floor trader said. "They'll follow it."

Corn opened the session lower but drew strength early from renewed commodity fund buying. Floor sources said funds bought 20 million bushels of corn on the day, adding to the estimated 100 million bushels purchased Tuesday.
Traders suggested the gains in new crop corn would buy acres away from soybeans, cutting into next year's supplies.
They noted the ratio between November soybean prices and December corn had narrowed to 2.47 to 1.0, premium soybeans.
The ratio had been as wide as 2.7 to 1.0 in December. Traders said the price comparison would favor corn planting because it makes corn more profitable than soybeans.
Increased farmer selling of soybeans following Tuesday's rally capped gains and pushed cash soymeal basis levels lower.
At 1130 CST, soybean meal was up $1.70 to $0.10 per ton with March up $0.70 at $256.40 a ton. Soyoil was down 0.07 cent per lb to up 0.06 with March off 0.01 at 23.91 cents.
